read: partial: main text pp.1-9 (abstract, introduction, related work, benchmark, EngJudge, construction, experiments, human study, conclusion, limitations, ethics) read in full; Appendix A (error analysis, p.12), B (benchmark details, pp.15-16), C.1 (penalty scales, p.17), D (score table, pp.19-20) and E (human study, pp.22-25) read; remaining appendices and prompts (pp.26-50) skimmed, including the per-stage judge prompts (pp.31-32).
venue_now: arXiv 2606.10833v1 [cs.AI], 9 Jun 2026 (page 1 stamp); no venue shown
what_it_is: EngVQA is a multimodal benchmark of 696 engineering problems with technical diagrams in five subjects (dynamics, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat and mass transfer, mechanics of materials), extracted from question PDFs and manually verified against the reference material (pp.1, 3, 6). Its evaluator, EngJudge, makes the model write an eight-stage tagged solution and scores each stage with a separate LLM-as-a-judge prompt that sees the reference solution, deducting severity-graded penalties, propagating upstream failures through a dependency graph and applying verbosity, coverage and sanity checks to give a 0-10 score (pp.4-6, 31-32). Two generators (Qwen3-VL-8B, Gemini-2.5-Flash) were evaluated; Gemini-2.5-Flash falls from 8.001 under a single-pass judge to 2.869 under EngJudge, and no generator exceeds a mean of 4 in any subject (pp.6-7). The reported human agreement (Pearson 0.975) compares the judge's scores with the same scores after raters' Likert adjustments of at most two points (pp.8, 22-24).
domain: engineering (multimodal, text plus diagrams): dynamics, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat and mass transfer, mechanics of materials; undergraduate and graduate level (pp.3, 15)
size: 696 problems: dynamics 171, thermodynamics 236, fluid mechanics 93, heat and mass transfer 96, mechanics of materials 100 (Table 2, p.3); two generator VLMs and two evaluator models (p.6)
source_of_items: existing academic problems from question PDFs (the source is not named), extracted with Adobe PDF Extract, PyMuPDF and Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite and manually verified against the reference material (pp.6, 9)
has_gold_traces: partial: each problem has a reference ('ground truth') solution from the source material, passed to every per-stage judge prompt and shown to the human raters (pp.7, 27, 31-32); there are no stage-level gold annotations and no gold intermediate values checked deterministically
evaluation: step-level or process, by LLM judge: eight required stages, each scored by a separate LLM-as-a-judge prompt (Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview primary, Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct second) with penalties of 2, 4, 7 or 10 points and fatal-error caps; the final-answer stage uses relative-error bands (no penalty within 5%, moderate 5-10%, major above 10%); dependency propagation and verbosity, coverage and physical-sanity meta-checks give a 0-10 score; 11 judge calls per solution (pp.4-6, 9)
human_validation: Items: extraction manually verified against the reference material (p.6). Evaluator: 9 undergraduate/graduate students each saw 4 randomly assigned problems with Gemini-2.5-Flash solutions (p.8). They first marked each step correct or incorrect without seeing the framework's output, but no agreement on those blind labels is reported (pp.22-23). They then saw EngJudge's score and justification and chose a 5-point Likert rating from 'much too low' to 'much too high'; the 'human' score is the judge's score plus -2 to +2 (Eqs. 11-12, p.23). Over 393 data points (285 stage, 108 meta-check) this gives Pearson 0.975 and MAE 0.67 (Table 11, p.23); 48.9% of points were rated 'about right' (p.25). The paper itself calls these 'synthetic human scores' (Fig. 11, p.24).
contamination_measures: none; the Limitations say contamination from pretraining data cannot be fully ruled out (p.9)

engtrace_use.explanation: Not cited in the May paper. Paragraph: engineering. EngVQA argues, as EngTrace does, that final-answer scoring hides reasoning failures, and it scores the stages of engineering solutions (pp.1, 4); with TPS-CalcBench and ThermoQA it falsifies the May claim that existing engineering benchmarks 'remain limited to outcome matching' (May p.3) and the introduction's 'no existing benchmark verifies this process' (May p.1). What EngTrace must say it adds: every EngVQA stage score is an LLM-judge output against a reference solution, with no deterministic check of intermediate values (p.5); its items are static and public; it forces an eight-stage output format (p.4); and its human validation is anchored on the judge's own scores (pp.22-24). EngTrace checks free-form traces against milestones computed by template code, recomputes displayed arithmetic, and validates its residual judge against labels from 15 experts.

suggested_wording: EngVQA (Wasiq et al., 2026) grades eight solution stages of 696 diagram-based problems in five mechanical subjects, but each stage is scored by an LLM judge against a reference solution.
facts_to_cite: 696 problems with technical diagrams in five subjects: dynamics 171, thermodynamics 236, fluid mechanics 93, heat and mass transfer 96, mechanics of materials 100 (Table 2, p.3).
Problems were extracted from question PDFs with Adobe PDF Extract, PyMuPDF and Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite and manually verified against the reference material (p.6).

EngJudge requires an eight-stage tagged solution (problem characterization, assumptions, visual interpretation, equation selection, logical reasoning, algebraic accuracy, physical interpretation, final answer) and scores each stage with a separate LLM-as-a-judge prompt, deducting 2/4/7/10-point penalties with fatal-error caps (pp.4-5).
The final-answer stage compares the predicted value with the ground truth by relative error: no penalty within 5%, a moderate penalty for 5-10%, a major penalty above 10% (p.5).
Stage scores are propagated through a dependency graph and adjusted by verbosity, coverage and physical-sanity checks to a 0-10 score (pp.5-6); evaluation takes 11 LLM judge calls per solution (p.9).
Two generators were evaluated (Qwen3-VL-8B, Gemini-2.5-Flash), with Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview as primary evaluator and Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct as a second (p.6).
Under a single-pass Gemini judge, Gemini-2.5-Flash scores 8.001; under EngJudge, 2.869; no generator exceeds a mean of 4 in any subject (p.7).

Human study: 9 undergraduate/graduate students, 4 randomly selected problems each; Pearson 0.975 and MAE 0.67 on a 10-point scale (p.8), where the human score is the judge's displayed score shifted by a Likert adjustment of -2 to +2, over 393 data points (Eqs. 11-12 and Table 11, p.23).
The Limitations state that contamination cannot be fully ruled out (p.9).
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares: engineering topics overlapping EngTrace's mechanical and chemical branches (fluid mechanics, mechanics of materials, thermodynamics, heat and mass transfer; Table 2, p.3); the argument that final answers hide reasoning failures (p.1); stage-level scoring with partial credit (pp.4-6); a human check of the evaluator (p.8). Lacks: generated instances (static set, p.6); gold intermediate values (reference solutions only, pp.31-32); deterministic step checks (every stage is judged by an LLM, p.5); free-form traces (the model must follow an eight-stage template, p.4); a blind validation of the evaluator (pp.22-24); contamination measures (p.9); breadth (two generators, p.6; no civil, electrical or industrial content). It is multimodal, which EngTrace is not.
notes: Paragraph: engineering (also usable in the judge-validity paragraph as an example of anchored validation). (1) Do not repeat the search note's 'Pearson 0.975 against 9 students' grades': the students did not grade independently; the 0.975 compares the judge's score with the same score after a Likert adjustment of at most two points (Eqs. 11-12, p.23), so a high correlation is close to guaranteed by construction. Cite EngVQA for its design, not for that number. (2) The abstract says 'multiple' VLMs were benchmarked; the experiments use two generators (p.6). (3) Internal inconsistency: dependency scoring preferred in 66.7% of cases (p.9) against 63.6% in Fig. 13 (p.25). (4) The two evaluators disagree widely under EngJudge: Qwen3-VL-8B's solutions score 0.416 overall from Qwen3-VL-32B and 1.670 from Gemini-3.1-Pro (Table 8, p.20). (5) Priority: must, because it is the most explicit claim of stage-wise evaluation of engineering reasoning; if the consolidator confines the paragraph to text-only benchmarks, TPS-CalcBench and ThermoQA carry the point and this drops to should.
